observations: Guest clock: after the restart inside the VM the guest clock ran about 9.5 minutes behind the host (VBox.log TM catch-up line: 572 s lag), so guest timestamps after the restart are early by that much (the AfterRestart driver-log line is stamped before the Install line). The restart check now compares uptimes and was unaffected; the wall-clock check used at Gate 17 would have given a false negative again.
Unpacking the package with the test harness took 1,440.9 s in the VM (843.7 s at Gate 17). This is the harness's Expand-Archive step, not the JARVIS installer, and is not a criterion.
Stopping a running JARVIS took 91.8 s at G6 (5.1 s at G4, 6.1 s at X3): inside the bound; still listed in docs/POST-CUTOVER-FIXES.md item 2.

result_statement: The packaged JARVIS 1.0.11 installs, starts, survives a Windows restart, uninstalls and reinstalls, updates from 1.0.10, rolls back, updates again, and recovers from an update killed in the middle of copying, with its data kept throughout, on a clean Windows 11 machine without administrator rights.
next: The same disc method and script are the standard check for every later release before it is offered to the everyday JARVIS (first: 1.0.12 with the fixes in docs/POST-CUTOVER-FIXES.md), each on the owner's word.
